newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban name U.N. representative.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban name U.N. representative.

text.p: The radical Islamic Taleban movement has appointed a former deputy foreign minister, Hamid Karzai, as Afghanistan's representative to the United Nations, a Taleban source said on Saturday.
Karzai will be challenging for a seat already occupied by Abdul Rahim Ghafoorzai, deputy foreign minister in the ousted government of president Burhanuddin Rabbani.

Karzai, who also served as deputy foreign minister under Rabbani, fled Kabul in 1994 when Rabbani's military chief Ahmad Shah Masood faced a revolt by former defence minister Abdul Rashid Dostum and former prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar.
Before fleeing to Pakistan, Karzai had been detained and manhandled by supporters of Masood, who is now allied with Dostum against the Taleban.
The Taleban, who seized Kabul on September 27, argue that since they control more than 75 percent of the country, their representative, not Ghafoorzai, should take the U.N. seat.
However, no country has yet officially recognised the Taleban as the Afghan government and the United Nations has deferred any decision on whether to eject Ghafoorzai.
